clue.text: Song and dance followed by commercial

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance
an ad is a commercial, a short advertisement

explanation.surface: A variety act: a song-and-dance routine, then a break for the adverts.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballad is a narrative song, often sentimental, so it is a kind of song.

clue.text: Remarkable as fish may be, unlike whales or dolphins

definitions.meaning: first meaning: extraordinary, out of the ordinary

definitions.text: as fish may be, unlike whales or dolphins
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the word fish can be ... in form, while whales and dolphins are plurals

explanation.walkthrough: The surface pretends to be zoology about fish versus sea mammals; it is grammar, since 'fish' looks the same in the singular and 'whales' and 'dolphins' are plural.
explanation.definitionFit: Singular means unusual or exceptional, and in grammar it names the number of a noun referring to one thing.

clue.text: Deny I had flipped in agreement

indicators.note: placed in something else, so these letters sit inside the word for agreement

parts.note: a contract is a formal agreement

indicators.note: something flipped is turned over, so the letters for 'I had' are read backwards

parts.note: I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: Someone backtracks: having flipped, they now deny what they had agreed to.
explanation.definitionFit: To contradict a statement is to assert its opposite, which is a way of denying it.

clue.text: Is a dosing ordered as result of this?

definitions.text: Is a dosing ordered as result of this?

indicators.note: ordered here means arranged into a fresh sequence, so the preceding letters are rearranged

parts.note: nine letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A doctor's prescription of medicine follows from identifying the illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ordered' reads as a doctor ordering a dose; it is also the signal to rearrange 'is a dosing', and the whole clue then describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A diagnosis identifies the illness, and a course of medication is prescribed as a consequence of it.

clue.text: Primarily weak, ineffective, mild person

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter of each following word is kept

parts.note: the initials of these four words

explanation.surface: A character sketch of a feeble, timid individual.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue serves both as the instruction to take initial letters and as a description of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A wimp is a feeble, timid person lacking courage, exactly what the description portrays.

clue.text: Part of hand that has slippery skin

definitions.meaning: first meaning: one fruit from a hand, the cluster in which these fruit grow
second meaning: the fruit whose discarded peel is the classic slapstick slip hazard

explanation.walkthrough: 'Part of hand' suggests a finger or thumb, but a hand is also a bunch of this fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Bananas grow in clusters called hands, and their peel is famously slippery underfoot.

clue.text: Part-time judge has request again about start of case

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the request word wraps around the single kept letter

parts.note: to reorder is to order, or request, once more

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of case

explanation.surface: A judge who sits only part of the time asks to rehear a case.
explanation.walkthrough: In England and Wales a recorder is a barrister or solicitor who sits as a judge part-time.
explanation.definitionFit: A recorder is the title of a part-time judge in the English courts, sitting in the Crown Court.

clue.text: Endlessly arid zone as part of US

indicators.note: endlessly means without an end, so each of the next three words loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A description of a parched desert region of the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' applies to all three words, so 'as' gives just its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Arizona is one of the fifty states that make up the United States, so it is a part of the country.

clue.text: Opposing something that goes with it

parts.note: a, the indefinite article, as in a something
gin and it is a cocktail, it being Italian vermouth

explanation.surface: Being against something that comes along with it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' here is Italian vermouth, as in the drink gin and it. Agin is a dialect form of 'against'.
explanation.definitionFit: Agin is a dialect or humorous word for against, so it means opposed to.

clue.text: Use as model I am sitting in front of current gallery

parts.note: I'm is the contraction of I am
I is the symbol for electric current
the Tate is the famous London art gallery

explanation.surface: An artist's model sits for a portrait in front of a gallery's current exhibition.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tate is a group of British national art galleries, Tate Britain and Tate Modern among them.
explanation.definitionFit: To imitate is to copy someone, taking them as your model or pattern.

clue.text: Settling around North very fast

indicators.note: around means encircling, so the first word wraps the letter for the compass point

parts.note: lighting on something is coming to rest or settling on it
N is the abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: A migrating bird settles quickly after heading north.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective lightning means extremely quick, as in a lightning raid, from the speed of a lightning flash.

clue.text: Philosopher inserting line in page, odd selection for author

indicators.note: inserting means putting something inside, so the line letter goes into the page word chain

parts.note: p is the abbreviation for page
L is the abbreviation for line

indicators.note: the odd selection means taking the first, third and fifth letters of the following word

parts.note: the odd-numbered letters of author

explanation.surface: A philosopher-author's text is being edited, a line added to a page.
explanation.walkthrough: Page plus the odd letters of 'author' give P and ATO, and the line letter is inserted between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Plato was the ancient Greek philosopher who wrote the Republic and taught Aristotle.

clue.text: Initially Delphi's extended mouthpiece?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Delphi is a Greek place, and its first letter in the Greek alphabet is this letter
second meaning: a wide, branching river mouth spreading out into the sea

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the oracle at Delphi speaking through a priestess; instead one meaning is the Greek letter for D and the other a spread-out river mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Delta is the fourth letter of the Greek alphabet, and also the fan-shaped mouth of a river such as the Nile.

clue.text: Where to find fruit or vegetable

parts.note: taken as written
chard is a leafy vegetable related to beet

explanation.surface: A shopper's question about which aisle has the fruit or the veg.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchard is a plot of fruit trees, so it is a place where fruit grows.

clue.text: Unfriendly when embracing attractive person in immature way

indicators.note: embracing means hugging, so the first word wraps around the next one

parts.note: a chilly welcome is an unfriendly one
a dish is slang for a good-looking person

explanation.surface: Someone acts coldly while hugging a good-looking partner, which seems juvenile.
explanation.definitionFit: To act childishly is to behave like a child, in a silly or immature manner.

clue.text: Once rule's broken, it's put in writing

indicators.note: something broken is smashed apart, so its letters can be put back in another order

parts.note: nine letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Once a rule has been broken, it gets recorded on paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put in writing' sounds like recording something, but it means put inside a letter alongside the written message.
explanation.definitionFit: An enclosure is an item placed inside an envelope with a letter, so it is put in with correspondence.

clue.text: I'm interfering so badly as member of government

indicators.note: done badly means done wrongly, so the letters come out in a muddled order

parts.note: fifteen letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A cabinet minister confesses to meddling clumsily.
explanation.walkthrough: Meddling in other countries' affairs fits the answer's job, which helps the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A foreign minister is the cabinet minister responsible for relations with other countries, so a government member.

clue.text: Dancing skill possibly OK for covering tango requirement

indicators.note: covering means wrapping round, so the jumbled letters surround the next item
possibly suggests one of several arrangements, so the preceding letters may be reordered

parts.note: five letters taken as written
it takes two to tango, as the saying goes

explanation.surface: A dance teacher says the steps are fine for the basics a tango needs.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'it takes two to tango' supplies the number needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Footwork is the skilful movement of the feet, a key accomplishment in dancing or sport.

clue.text: After short voyage North with one parent, land in Caribbean

indicators.note: short means cut down, so the word for voyage loses its last letter

parts.note: a trip is a journey or voyage
N is the abbreviation for north
I is the Roman numeral one
dad is an informal word for a father

explanation.surface: A traveller sails north with a parent and lands on a Caribbean island.
explanation.definitionFit: Trinidad is the larger island of Trinidad and Tobago, a country in the southern Caribbean.

clue.text: Said to include section of round-the-world trip

indicators.note: to include something is to hold it inside, so the first word wraps around the second

parts.note: oral means spoken rather than written
a bit is a part or section

explanation.surface: A traveller describes part of a journey around the globe.
explanation.definitionFit: Orbital describes a path circling a body such as the Earth, so it relates to a trip round the world.

clue.text: Game for which paired opponents appear in answer

definitions.text: Game for which paired opponents appear in answer

parts.words: Game for which paired opponents appear in answer
parts.note: surface reading: a game in which a pair of rivals turn up in reply to something
setter's reading: a card game played by two partnerships facing each other across the table

explanation.walkthrough: The setter points to a card game played by two partnerships of two, each pair opposing the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Bridge is a card game for four players in two partnerships, so the opponents come in pairs.

clue.text: Doctor needing medical help that's often boring

parts.note: Dr is the abbreviation for doctor
someone ill is unwell and in need of treatment

explanation.surface: A sick doctor whose company is tedious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boring' seems to mean dull, but it means making holes.
explanation.definitionFit: A drill is a tool used for boring holes in wood, metal or teeth.

clue.text: Suitable flower planted around Kew, mostly

indicators.note: planted around means set on all sides, so the flower word surrounds the shortened place name

parts.note: the lily is a flower

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the place name loses its last letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A fitting bloom has been planted in Kew, the London botanic gardens.
explanation.walkthrough: Kew Gardens is the Royal Botanic Gardens in south-west London, which suits the flower surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A likely candidate is a suitable or promising one, a common sense of the adjective.

clue.text: German musical family's group losing heart

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letter, and losing it means dropping that middle

parts.note: a batch is a group or set

explanation.surface: A German family of musicians loses its spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bachs were a dynasty of German composers and performers, with Johann Sebastian the most famous member.

clue.text: Carefully consider, in manner of speaking?

indicators.note: speaking refers to the spoken word, so the answer only matches the word for manner when spoken

parts.note: a way is a manner of doing something

explanation.surface: Someone thinks hard about how they talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In manner of speaking' reads as a stock phrase, but splits into the word for manner and the sound signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To weigh a matter is to assess it carefully, balancing one side against the other.

clue.text: Nelson, for example, in part of ship

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a nelson is a wrestling grip
second meaning: the space below decks where cargo is stored

explanation.walkthrough: 'Nelson' and 'ship' point to Admiral Nelson, but a nelson here is a wrestling grip, such as the full nelson.
explanation.definitionFit: A nelson is a type of grip in wrestling, and the cargo space in a ship's hull is also so named.

clue.text: Cronies, having performed turn, remain for comedy act

indicators.note: performing a turn means swinging round, so the word for cronies is read backwards

parts.note: pals are close friends
to stick is to stay put

explanation.surface: Friends finish their variety turn and stay on for a comic routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn' looks like a stage act, which fits the comedy surface, but it is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Slapstick is boisterous physical comedy, full of pratfalls and custard pies.

clue.text: Soldier's uniform

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a professional soldier in a standing army; the 's is read as 'is'
second meaning: even, consistent, the same throughout

explanation.walkthrough: 'Uniform' suggests what a soldier wears, but here it is an adjective meaning even; the 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A regular is a full-time professional soldier, and regular also means steady and evenly consistent.

clue.text: Alternative to case contributing to foolish old allegations

indicators.note: contributing to means forming part of, so the answer is found within the following words

parts.note: spans the end of the first word, all of the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A suitcase figures in some silly, outdated accusations.
explanation.definitionFit: A holdall is a large soft bag for travel, used instead of a suitcase.
